response_text: To pass an argument into a thread, the user first needs to define their thread function to accept a single void* argument. If multiple arguments are needed, the user can group them into a struct and pass a pointer to the struct instead. The OS then modifies the osCreateThread function to fill the R0 register with a pointer to the user’s data. This works because input arguments to functions are passed via registers R0 through R3, and a void* can be cast to an int and stored in R0. When the thread runs, it can acst the void* argument back to the appropriate type and dereference it to access the data.\n
